MA-S4:unknown_rhetorical_moves:Entity activation via semantic bridging performs iterative propagation of entity relevance through the sentence–entity subgraph based on query–sentence similarity, identifying latent intermediate entities for multi-hop connections. The system trades relational expressiveness for robustness and simplicity: retrieval quality is recovered through the propagation mechanism rather than through edge typing, and the absence of typed edges constitutes a deliberate scoping decision rather than a gap in the design.,The first retrieval stage activates relevant entities through local semantic bridging over a bipartite entity–sentence–passage hierarchy in which no typed relation edges are present. Entity nodes connect to the sentence node in which they appear, and sentence nodes connect to their parent passage node; the graph topology is derived entirely from structural co-occurrence rather than from predicted or rule-based relation labels. This design omits a dedicated relation-extraction module, so the retrieval signal is carried by score propagation through the structural topology rather than by edge semantics. Propagation is governed by two guard conditions: the iteration loop continues only while `len(current_entities) > 0 and iteration < self.config.max_iterations`, and candidate entities are pruned when `entity_score < self.config.iteration_threshold`.,The stage operates in three sequential phases: initialization, iterative propagation, and dynamic pruning. Initialization assigns seed scores from query–sentence similarity; iterative propagation expands the active frontier through the structural graph; dynamic pruning discards entities whose scores fall below the configured threshold, terminating the loop when no active entities remain or the maximum iteration count is reached.,`LinearRAG.calculate_entity_scores` propagates entity relevance through breadth-first frontier expansion: at each iteration the current frontier of active entities seeds a new frontier of adjacent entities in the sentence–entity subgraph, and scores are attenuated as they travel outward. The propagation mechanism formalizes how query–sentence similarity initializes seed scores and how those scores diffuse across the structural topology to identify latent intermediate entities for multi-hop connections. The closed-form derivation of the per-iteration score update is deferred pending resolution of the formula obligation.
